findings.title: The default-vs-off A/B collapses to the same arm for the default model (a `:off:off` double suffix and a mislabeled 'default' row)
findings.detail: `DEFAULT_MODELS` now contains `DEFAULT_REVIEW_MODEL` (scripts/bench-review-models.ts:26), which this same diff changed to `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash:off` (extensions/review.ts:87). The arm loop builds `const childModel = arm === "default" ? model : `${model}:${arm}`;` (line 65) with the default arms `["default", "off"]` (line 50). For the deepseek entry that yields: arm "default" → `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash:off` (thinking off, i.e. *the same configuration as the other arm*, but reported under the "default" column) and arm "off" → `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash:off:off`, a doubly-suffixed id that is not a real model. Consequence: the default-vs-default-thinking A/B that the new doc comment and README line 63 cite as the justification ("100% recall … at ~1/4 the wall time of the same model with default thinking (which now exceeds the 6m finder cap)") cannot be reproduced by this script for the model it is about — the headline comparison degenerates into two identical (or one failed) rows. The `it` contains no expectation, so even a table full of `FAILED:` rows passes; the only protection is the author eyeballing the markdown. Not covered by any other test: the whole script is excluded from `npm test` by its filename (no root vitest config, default include is `**/*.{test,spec}.*`), so nothing exercises it.
findings.recommendation: Strip an existing thinking suffix before appending the arm (`const base = model.replace(/:(off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max)$/, "")` and use `base` for both arms), or drop the suffixed default from DEFAULT_MODELS so the list is plain provider/id values.

findings.title: Untrusted tool output is copied raw into the judge's prompt, and the judge's verdict then steers the agent in the harness's voice
findings.detail: Still valid; goal.ts is untouched by this diff. buildSettleJudgeTask splices `## Digest of the agent's recent work (oldest first, clipped)\n${ctx.workDigest}` verbatim (extensions/goal.ts:854), and the settle-triage twin does the same. buildWorkDigest (goal.ts:765-821) fills that digest from assistant notes, tool-call arguments and tool-result text (WORK_DIGEST_MAX_CHARS = 6_000), i.e. content that untrusted repo files and command output can influence. The only boundary is an agent instruction telling the child to treat the digest as data (SETTLE_JUDGE_AGENT instruction list, goal.ts:833), and the parsed verdict (parseSettleVerdict, goal.ts:693) is consumed as the harness's own decision — `complete` steers the parent to summarize and call goal complete, `blocked` steers it to declare an impasse, `verify`/`continue` drives the settle — so text injected through command output can influence the agent's next step in the harness's voice.
findings.recommendation: Fence the digest and previousReason as an explicitly delimited untrusted block (e.g. <work-digest>…</work-digest>) and restate the data-only boundary after the block, not only in the agent instructions.

findings.title: The judge's task — a 6 KB digest of session content, including tool output — is passed to the child as a command-line argument
findings.detail: Carried; still valid, unchanged. `createLlmSettleJudge` passes `buildSettleJudgeTask(goal, ctx)` as the task (goal.ts:896, options at goal.ts:902); the default runner spawns `pi` via `buildChildArgs`, which appends the task after `--` (extensions/subagents.ts:326-345). The task embeds up to 6,000 chars of session content — assistant notes, the JSON arguments of commands the agent ran (any credential passed inline on a bash command), and their output — so that text sits in the process command line for the whole judge timeout at every turn end (world-readable `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` on Linux, captured by process accounting/EDR). Separately, the `idleTimeoutMs: 0` exemption on the same line is not asserted by any test (tests/goal.test.ts records only timeoutMs/signal), so dropping it would not fail the suite.
findings.recommendation: Feed the judge/triage task on stdin or a temp file instead of argv (runChild already spawns with stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe']); at minimum cap the assembled task bytes.

findings.title: The parent's idle window is a fixed 5m that no longer matches the child's own (configurable) HTTP idle timeout, so a healthy child on a slow local model is still SIGKILLed as a 'dead request'
findings.detail: Carried; still valid. `DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000` (subagents.ts:38) is what any run that omits `idleTimeoutMs` gets through `resolveIdleTimeoutMs` (subagents.ts:76-78), and the `subagent`/`subagents` tools pass only `parseIdleTimeoutMs(process.env)` (subagents.ts:962, :1039) with no per-task or per-agent override. The child pi process's HTTP idle timeout is a user setting with its own choices (30s/1m/2m/5m/disabled — `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/http-dispatcher.js:7-11`, `dist/core/settings-manager.js:77`), so a user who raises or disables it for a slow local model still has the parent SIGKILL the child after 5m of silence inside one LLM wait, reported as `stalled: no output for Ns (request likely dead)`; the only remedy is the process-wide `PI_SUBAGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, which loosens detection for every child.
findings.recommendation: Derive the default from the run's budget (e.g. options.idleTimeoutMs ?? Math.min(DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, Math.max(60_000, timeoutMs / 2))) and/or add a per-task idle override so one slow child can be exempted without loosening all of them.

findings.title: parseIdleTimeoutMs still accepts any positive value, so a sub-tick window (2.9, or 300 meant as seconds) SIGKILLs every child on the first tick
findings.detail: Carried; still valid. The positive branch returns the raw number unclamped (`return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS;`, subagents.ts:70), `resolveIdleTimeoutMs` forwards it unchanged (:76-78), the watchdog only gates on `idleMs > 0` and its tick floor is `Math.max(100, Math.min(5_000, Math.floor(idleMs / 4)))`. Since `lastActivityAt` is initialized at spawn, any window at or below the 100 ms tick kills every child before it can emit its first stdout line, and the caller sees `stalled: no output for 1s (request likely dead)` with no hint that the env value caused it; `PI_SUBAGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=300` (meant as seconds) behaves the same in practice. The values are pinned as correct in tests (`"2.9" === 2.9`, tests/subagents.test.ts), while the sibling knob in this repo clamps (`clampInt(env.PI_REVIEW_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, 5 * 60_000, 10_000, 6 * 60 * 60_000)`, extensions/review.ts:137).
findings.recommendation: Clamp the positive branch to a sane floor (e.g. Math.max(10_000, n)) and update the '1500'/'2.9' expectations so the tests pin the guard.

findings.title: gitDiff runs with execFile's default 1 MiB maxBuffer, so a large commit aborts the bench before any child runs
findings.detail: `execFileAsync("git", ["show", commit, "--format=", "--no-color", "-U3"])` uses execFile's default `maxBuffer` of 1 MiB; a commit whose diff exceeds that (the repo's own cached eval diffs at `scripts/eval/data/diffs/` reach megabytes, and `BENCH_COMMIT`/the positional accept any commit-ish) rejects with `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER`. The rejection is not caught anywhere — only the per-arm `runChild` call is wrapped in try/catch (line 67) — so the run dies with a child-process error before a single timing is produced, even though the diff is truncated to the finder's byte budget by `fitTask` immediately afterwards.
findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit bound, e.g. `execFileAsync("git", [...], { maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 })`, and/or wrap `gitDiff` so a failure names the commit (`throw new Error(\`git show ${commit} failed: ${err.message}\`)`) instead of surfacing a raw maxBuffer error.

findings.title: The documented positional commit argument cannot reach the test under vitest — the bench would time the hardcoded 19488b1 (or die in `git show`)
findings.detail: The header advertises `npm run bench:review-models [commit-ish]`, but the value is read as `process.argv[2]`. Vitest does not hand the caller's positional argument to a test: it consumes positional CLI tokens itself as test-name/file filters (an unmatched filter aborts the run), and the fork worker that actually executes the file does not receive them, so `process.argv[2]` is either `"run"` (vitest's own subcommand, defined, so the `?? "19488b1"` fallback never fires and `git show run` fails) or `undefined` (fallback to the hardcoded `19488b1`, silently benching a commit the caller did not ask for). Every other benchmark in this repo takes such inputs from the environment only (scripts/bench-recall.ts:47-54, scripts/warm-store.ts:29), none read argv.
findings.recommendation: Drop the argv path from both the code and the doc comment and make `BENCH_COMMIT` the only way to pick the commit (failing loudly when it is absent rather than defaulting to a stale sha).

findings.title: Tests assert the absence of a before_agent_start handler (harness detail) rather than observable behavior
findings.detail: Still valid, and outside this diff's files only in location — the assertions are untouched by the review-model change. Both assertions (tests/recall.test.ts:1152 in "sends the reminder at the compaction commit…" and :2415 in "delivers the compaction trigger through ctx.compact, never a run-start hook") check `events.get("before_agent_start") === undefined`, i.e. that `registerRecallTool` never called `pi.on('before_agent_start', …)` — a mechanism of the test double. The behavior the change is about (no reminder/compaction is injected at run start) is covered nearby by `expect(compactCalls).toHaveLength(0)` (:2412) and `expect(sent).toHaveLength(1)` (:1142), which are the assertions that would actually catch a regression; the registration check would instead fail spuriously on any refactor that registers a differently-purposed before_agent_start handler (recall registers several other events), while still not proving a run-start injection never reaches the agent.
findings.recommendation: Assert the observable effect (e.g. that no message is returned/mutated for the agent at run start) or drop the registration assertion and keep the positive 'reminder is sent at commit' checks.
